record.original_question: Let F be a known plane region representing a forest. Find a parametrized curve C such that, no matter which point P of F a hiker starts from and no matter which initial direction the hiker faces, every curve congruent to C with initial point P eventually leaves F; among all such guaranteed-escape curves, which one minimizes the worst-case escape time, equivalently the length of the shortest trajectory that guarantees escape?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Let F be a plane region that we will call forest. Find a parametrized curve C such that (1) for every P ∈ F, for every curve C̃ congruent to C and with initial point P, C̃ “scapes from F” (it is not contained in F) and (2) among them find the “best” possible one.
Here by “best” we will interpret the shortest time of escape in the worst case or, in other words, the shortest trajectory that guarantees to escape.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F ⊂ ℝ² be a fixed, known plane region (the "forest"). A parametrized curve C: [0, L] → ℝ² is said to guarantee escape from F if, for every starting point P ∈ F and every rigid motion (translation and rotation) sending the initial point C(0) to P, the resulting congruent image C̃ of C is not entirely contained in F (i.e. C̃ exits F at some parameter value).

Among all parametrized curves C that guarantee escape from F in this sense, determine one that minimizes the arc length L (equivalently, the worst-case time/distance until escape, assuming unit speed). That is, find

  inf { length(C) : C guarantees escape from F },

and exhibit an optimal curve achieving (or approaching) this infimum, for a given forest shape F — and, more ambitiously, give a procedure that produces such an optimal curve for an arbitrary plane region F.
artifact.status_search_result: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, posed in 1955–1956, remains open in general. Optimal escape paths are known for a handful of special forest shapes (e.g. infinite strips, half-planes, circles, certain rectangles and some convex regions), but no general solution for arbitrary plane regions has been verified. A 2024 arXiv preprint by Z. Deng proposes a general framework, but it is not established as a community-accepted solution and the problem is still listed as open (e.g. on Wikipedia and related surveys).

status_evidence.title: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A general solution to the problem... remains an open problem. Solutions are known in specific cases including circles, infinite strips and certain rectangles.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is generally still open, with solutions only for special forest shapes.

status_evidence.title: A General Solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-forest Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a framework reducing discretized versions to traveling salesman / Hamiltonian path variants; claims consistency with known special cases.
status_evidence.claim: A 2024 preprint proposes a general approach but is a recent unrefereed contribution.

status_evidence.title: Bellman's Escape Problem for Convex Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses partial results for convex polygonal forests.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available for restricted classes of forests.
